rationale:
ROUND 3 of 7ba5b8c4. Round 2 was REVISE (5 approve / 3 object) BUT NOTE unreadable:1 -- `editquality`, one of the two always-run seats and the seat that found round 1's real defect, produced unparseable output and its verdict is LOST (bugs_open/119). The REVISE stands on the other seats' merits, so this round answers those; the missing seat is flagged, not used as an excuse.

TWO OF bug_historian'S OBJECTIONS ARE DESIGN DEFECTS AND ARE FIXED IN CODE, NOT IN PROSE.

(A) THE GUARD WAS SCOPED TO THE WRONG FAILURE SHAPE, and the proof is round 1 itself. My WARN fired only on sections==0. Round 1's actual defect -- the register glob catching 28 planning docs and missing 110 register entries -- produced a NON-ZERO, PLAUSIBLE count from the wrong source. bug_historian: 'the guard as specified would not have caught the very defect this round's rationale spends four paragraphs proving happened.' That is exactly right and it is the sharpest thing said about this plan. Fixed three ways: per-glob counts are now logged and returned (a total hides a source contributing zero); ANY configured glob matching zero files is a HARD ERROR, not a warn; and the path-shape assertion moves INTO the action so it re-runs every index, rather than living only in a VERIFY a human runs once at merge time.

I want to be honest about the limit: no runtime guard can know I meant register/ rather than its parent. What is now standing is (i) a glob that matches nothing fails loudly and (ii) per-glob counts are visible every run. I have DELETED a third claim from this paragraph before submitting: I had written that a run-over-run drift check flags a material change in any glob's contribution, and NO SKETCH IN THIS PLAN IMPLEMENTS ONE. Claiming a mechanism the plan does not contain is the precise defect that put this workstream here -- 'the indexer is already walking the file' -- so it is removed rather than quietly implemented later. The prune floor in edit 5 is a total-count collapse guard, not a per-glob drift check, and is described as what it is. Round 1's defect would have been caught by (ii) -- 28 sections from a source expected to contribute ~110 is visible the moment the number is printed per glob instead of summed away.

(B) THE SHARED PRUNE CAN DESTROY GOOD DOC ROWS. bug_historian cites the historian pattern almost verbatim: 'the identical DELETE+INSERT rebuild pattern destroyed a working A* pathfinding game; recurred independently on a second site.' If a future run has files_read==0 (glob typo, moved directory, permissions) the WARN path does not fire and the shared prune deletes the previous run's good doc rows. Fixed: the prune is now kind-aware and refuses to delete kind='doc' rows when this run produced fewer than half the stored doc count. The run still upserts; it declines to destroy. A refusal is reported and logged loudly rather than passing silently.

THE ABSENCE CLAIM IS NOW A SEARCH WITH METHODOLOGY, answering prior_art (medium): 'one found instance does not establish only'. Correct -- round 2 showed a file:line, not a search. Run now: `grep -rnE '^func [A-Za-z_]*([Cc]hunk|[Ss]plit|[Ss]ection|[Hh]eading|[Pp]arseDoc|[Ee]xtractSec)[A-Za-z_]*\(' --include=*.go . | grep -v docs/ | grep -v _test.go` -> 90 hits. Triaged: chunkContent (rag_actions.go:396) is the only CHUNKER; ~80 are *Section* functions about PAGE sections (site building, page_components, HTML), a different domain; the rest are splitSymbol/splitScope/SplitCodeRequestKey/splitDecl etc.

AND THE SEARCH FOUND A NEAR-MISS ROUND 2 HAD MISSED, which is the point of being made to do it: `extractProductSection(markdown string)` at vet_med_price_scrape_action.go:650 IS markdown-aware AND heading-aware. Examined: it is a TRUNCATOR, not a splitter -- it scans a fixed allow-list of end-markers ('## description', 'related products', ...), takes the earliest, and returns ONE prefix string. It cannot enumerate headings, records no line spans, and its marker list is specific to product pages. Not reusable, for a stated reason rather than by omission.

reuse_agent (low) asked whether a markdown PARSER is already a dependency. Checked: goldmark appears in go.sum ONLY, and every entry is '/go.mod'-suffixed -- module-graph entries with no source hash. It is absent from go.mod's require and imported nowhere in our code. So there is no parser to reuse; adding one would be a new direct dependency for a job a single-pass line scanner does.

guardian (low, edit 4) asked which pipeline OWNS the indexer. Named from live config: agent `code-indexer`, step `index_symbols`, action `index_code_symbols`, spawned by `index-orchestrator`, fired by scheduled task `code-index-refresh` every 86400s. That pipeline absorbs the ~1,749-row/+35% growth and the embedding cost, and it is a dedicated indexing lane -- not a shared user-facing pipeline.

prior_art (low, edit 6) was right that my 243 precedent claim should be checked, not restated. Checked with `git log -S`: the old COALESCE predicate entered 243's VERIFY in 37f7deff9 and was removed in fd3edfb5b -- so the file did carry an assertion pinned to superseded code, as claimed.

debug_historian (low) notes the migration RAISEs on rerun rather than being a 0-row no-op. Accepted as stated: for a DDL constraint swap there is no partial-row state to leave dangling, but it is not the documented shape and a rerun therefore looks like a hard failure rather than a silent pass. Named in the migration header.

plan.summary: ROUND 3. D11 layer 1b: index MARKDOWN sections from four durable prose sources into code_symbols, reusing layer 1's body column and content search. Round 3 fixes two DESIGN defects bug_historian found: the fail-loud guard was scoped to all-zero when the real defect was non-zero-but-wrong-source (now per-glob counts + a zero-match glob is a hard error + the scope check runs in the action every index), and the shared prune could destroy good doc rows on a future collapse (now a kind-aware prune floor that refuses to delete). Absence claims are now searches with methodology attached.

edits.rationale: code_symbols.kind carries a CHECK permitting Go kinds ONLY, so a markdown row cannot be inserted at all -- the mechanical blocker. Verbatim from the live DB: CHECK ((kind = ANY (ARRAY['func'::text, 'method'::text, 'struct'::text, 'interface'::text, 'alias'::text, 'type'::text, 'var'::text, 'const'::text]))). Adds 'doc'. READERS enumerated for guardian (round 1, medium): no reader switches on kind; diagnose_code_lookup never selects it; scanCodeSymbolRows selects it into lookup_code_symbols' result map only. NUMBER MOVES -- 253 is highest today, but this workstream's last migration was approved as 241 and shipped as 243 because two sessions took 241 and 242 inside four hours. Re-read the max immediately before writing the file.

ROUND 2, answering debug_historian (medium): the needle-gate discipline wants verify AND rollback as separate files, and this constraint relaxation is what makes the Go writer's INSERTs possible at all -- so a bad flattenMarkdown run had no scripted recovery. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS FILE IS NOT TRIVIAL: the old CHECK cannot be restored while kind='doc' rows exist, so the rows must be deleted FIRST or the ALTER fails with a check-violation on existing data. Written as one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable.

ROUND 3, rewritten for bug_historian (medium): the round-2 guard fired only on a TOTAL of zero, and round 1's real defect was non-zero-but-wrong-source. Now: counts are tracked PER GLOB and returned; a glob matching ZERO FILES is a hard error (the plan's only fail-loud escalation, because a source contributing nothing is indistinguishable from a source that does not exist); and the scope/path-shape assertion runs HERE, every index, not only in a VERIFY a human runs once. NOT REUSING, with the search attached in the rationale: chunkContent (rag_actions.go:396) is a fixed-width window; extractProductSection (vet_med_price_scrape_action.go:650) is markdown- and heading-aware but TRUNCATES at a fixed end-marker list and returns one prefix with no spans; no markdown parser is a dependency (goldmark is go.sum-graph-only, absent from go.mod, imported nowhere). Suffix determinism, for guardian (low): the counter is a per-file map[string]int incremented during ONE top-to-bottom pass over the file's own lines, so the Nth occurrence gets the same suffix every run -- document order, never map iteration order.

content does THREE jobs -- trigram text, the EMBEDDED text, and the input to content_hash which is the re-embed trigger. composeSymbolContent keeps the code BODY out for exactly this reason; markdown must obey the same rule or the first reindex re-embeds all 4,992 existing rows plus the new ones. So content is heading + path only; the section text goes to body, which is what the content check now searches anyway.

ROUND 3, adding the prune floor for bug_historian (medium): the shared prune (DELETE WHERE repo=$1 AND commit_sha IS DISTINCT FROM $2) covers both kinds, so a future run that yields few or no doc rows -- files_read==0 from a moved directory, so the WARN path never fires -- would let the prune delete the previous run's good doc rows. That is the DELETE+INSERT-rebuild-destroys-working-content pattern the historian cites. The prune is now kind-aware and REFUSES to delete kind='doc' rows when this run produced under half the stored doc count: the run still upserts, it declines to destroy, and the refusal is logged and returned rather than passing silently. THE GLOBS ARE THE DESIGN and round 1 got one wrong: the register lives at register/*.md (110 entries), not the top level (28 superseded planning docs). Owning pipeline, for guardian (low): agent code-indexer, step index_symbols, spawned by index-orchestrator, fired by scheduled task code-index-refresh every 86400s -- a dedicated indexing lane, so the +35% growth and embedding cost land there and nowhere user-facing.

A SUPPLEMENT, not a fix -- explicitly conceding editquality (low, edit 6): this file changes no behaviour and is not counted as covering any mechanism. It exists because 243's VERIFY caught a real defect in layer 1 that a reviewer had been asked to eyeball. Carries the 243 lesson forward: that file's EXPLAIN stayed pinned to the OLD predicate after the code changed, so it reported on a query nobody ran while presenting as coverage -- these assertions must be re-read whenever flattenMarkdown or the globs change.

plan.risks: (1) THE ONE INVARIANT, unchanged: content and content_hash must not gain section text, or every existing row re-embeds. composeDocContent is heading+path only; the VERIFY asserts hash integrity across ALL rows. (2) EMBEDDING COST IS REAL AND NEW: ~1,749 rows each embed once on first index. Layer 1's cost was zero-by-construction; this one is not, and it is stated rather than buried. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: measured at 1 today. The suffix counter runs in document order over a single top-to-bottom pass, so it is stable across runs -- if a reviewer can show a path where it is not, the prune/upsert churns those rows every index. (4) SCOPE IS THE DESIGN AND ROUND 1 GOT IT WRONG ONCE ALREADY: the register glob pointed at 28 superseded planning docs instead of 110 register entries. That is the failure mode in miniature -- a wrong glob poisons the corpus with exactly the stale-doc class the plan exists to keep out, while every counter reports success. The VERIFY's out-of-scope assertion and the register_sections check are the guards, and the Go comment marks the value load-bearing. (5) BLAST RADIUS OF THE CHECK CHANGE, now enumerated rather than assumed: no reader switches on kind; the only behavioural change is that a doc row can appear in lookup_code_symbols' top-k. (6) ROLLBACK ORDER: the old CHECK is validated against existing data, so kind='doc' rows must be deleted BEFORE the constraint is restored -- the sidecar does both in one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable. (7) DEPLOY: Go is inert until the image rolls, so the CHECK relaxes immediately and markdown simply does not arrive until then -- a degrade, not a break. Confirm against the RUNNING pod with a string this change creates plus one it deletes, never git and never the tag. (8) The freshness banner keys on the indexed COMMIT (108 defect A, live v1.0.1189), so a prose answer carries the same staleness qualifier a code answer does.
